slides.title: Where has this water come from?
What happens when materials are cooled?
bullets: When a gas is cooled, particles slow down and come together — this is CONDENSING (gas → liquid).
When a liquid is cooled further, particles lock into a fixed arrangement — this is FREEZING (liquid → solid).
Changing state is REVERSIBLE — the same material can be heated or cooled to change back again.

slides.title: Where do we see this in the real world?
bullets: The water cycle uses the same state changes: evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.
This links to Geography — the water cycle moves water around our planet using these exact processes.
The same water changes state over and over — it is never destroyed, only transformed.

sections.text: Use the diagram below. Write the correct process name in each arrow and add the temperature.
Write one or two sentences explaining why changing state is called reversible. Use the word bank.

sections.words: reversible  •  melt  •  freeze  •  evaporate  •  condense  •  solid  •  liquid  •  gas  •  heat  •  cool  •  the same material

sections.text: Arrow 1: Solid to Liquid = MELTING at 0°C
Arrow 2: Liquid to Solid = FREEZING at 0°C
Arrow 3: Liquid to Gas   = EVAPORATING / BOILING at 100°C
Arrow 4: Gas to Liquid   = CONDENSING at 100°C
Changing state is reversible because the same material can be heated or cooled to move between solid, liquid and gas. No new substance is made and the process can go in both directions.
